summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, K. L. Dhammajoti studied at the University of Kelaniya and under Yinshun and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa. He taught at Kelaniya, held posts at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and was a chair at Calgary.

Kumataro Kawada was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Tokyo Imperial University and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Japan Women's University and the University of Tokyo, and later became professor emeritus at Komazawa University.
Kumja Paik Kim is a specialist in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology who earned her doctorate from Stanford University. In 1989, she served as curator of Korean art at the Asian Art Museum.

Kumkum Bandyopadhyay works in history and archaeology, having completed doctoral studies under Rupendra Kumar Chattopadhyay. Bandyopadhyay held an attested post as a research scholar and fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

Kun Chang was a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist who studied at Tsinghua University and Yale University under Franklin Edgerton and Geshe Nornang. He held academic posts at Academia Sinica, the University of Washington, and UC Berkeley (1963–1987).

Kunio Harikai is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed his BA and PhD degrees at Kyushu University, studying under Seiren Matsunami and Shōren Ihara. He served as an associate professor at Saga Medical School from circa 1978 to 1993.
Kunio Iwaya studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1962 to 1970. He later held a post at Meiji Gakuin University from around 1975 to 2014.

Kunio Mugitani is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Mitsuji Fukunaga between 1970 and 1976. He served as a professor at Kyoto University and its Institute for Research in Humanities from circa 1991 to 2013.
Kunio Odaka studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1928 to 1931. He later held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1945–1969) and Sophia University (~1969–1978).

Kunio Yanagita studied law at the University of Tokyo (~1897–1900) before working in religious studies and Japanology. He served in the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce, Keio University, the Privy Council, and Kokugakuin University (~1947–1952).

Kuno Fischer was a philosopher who studied at the University of Leipzig and the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held academic posts at the University of Jena from circa 1856 to 1872 and at Heidelberg University from circa 1872 to 1906.

Kuno Lorenz is a philosopher who studied at several universities, earning his PhD at Kiel and habilitation at Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held the chair of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1970) and was a professor at Saarland University (1974–1998).

Kuno Meyer was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig under Ernst Windisch. He held academic posts at the University of Liverpool (~1884–1911) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1911–1919).

Kuntala Bhattacharya is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Jadavpur University under Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra, and completed an MA under Prabal Kumar Sen. She held an attested post at Rabindra Bharati University in 2009.
Kunzang Namgyal studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and later taught Terton Sogyal.

Kunzang Pelden studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Thubten Chökyi Dorje, and Patrul Rinpoche. He taught several figures, including Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.

Kurt A. Behrendt is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles. Around 2006, he served as an assistant curator in the Department of Asian Art at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
Kurt Andrew Johnson is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of York by 2010 under the supervision of Jane Moody.

Kurt Huber was a philosopher who earned his PhD at the University of Munich (~1913–1917). He went on to serve on the faculty at the University of Munich as an außerordentlicher Professor in 1926 and full professor in 1938.

Kurt Tropper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner. He has held posts as a Vertragsassistent at the University of Vienna and at the Austrian Academy of Sciences.
